findings.evidence: Lines 158–166 define and characterize only `capMatching`, while the roadmap names `middleLoopCount` and lines 27–29 describe loops as alternating caps of the upper diagram with cups of the lower diagram.
findings.fix: Add a `cupMatching` on `{j // D.IsCup (Sum.inr j)}` with its characteristic endpoint lemma and normal-form annotations, parallel to `capMatching`.
findings.issue: Only `capMatching` is exposed, but middle-loop traversal also needs the parallel perfect matching on `topCup`; consumers otherwise must reconstruct it from `D.val`.

findings.evidence: The implementation’s general characterization `stackVal_eq_of_exit` is private at lines 224–233; public value lemmas at lines 285–365 specialize only exit times 0, 1, and 2, while `compose_assoc` is the next roadmap target (`README.md:403–405`).
findings.fix: Expose a general relational/reachability characterization of `(composeDiagram D₁ D₂).val x = y` (with usable introduction and elimination forms) sufficient to prove arbitrary strand behavior and associativity without unfolding private walking machinery.
findings.issue: The opaque `composeDiagram` has no general elimination theorem describing an arbitrary composite strand; the six public value lemmas cover only exits after at most three arcs, so longer alternating middle paths cannot be analyzed through the public API.

findings.evidence: Theorems at lines 443 and 458 state exact left/right identity rewrite rules but have no automation annotation.
findings.issue: The two identity normalization theorems are not tagged `@[simp]`, so expressions composing with the identity diagram do not normalize automatically.

summary: The public surface lacks the general strand API needed by the roadmap’s next operations, including the matching on middle cups and a complete characterization of composition.
